merger_description:
Sumitomo Mitsui Trust Bank, Limited (**SMTB**) is a Japan-based provider of financial services. In Australia, SMTB provides commercial lending services, including general corporate loans, fund financing, and property finance. SMTB’s commercial lending services are mainly conducted through offshore booking transactions by SMTB's Singapore Branch.

SMTB also provides ‘trust banking services’ to Australia-based customers, which are a combination of traditional banking functions and fiduciary services, with a particular focus on fee-based business such as asset management and trust administration, often serving long-term institutional clients. SMTB has a registered office in Sydney, which is focussed only on local market research.

The IFM SuMi TRUST ANZ Debt Fund (the **Trust**) is a ‘fund-of-one’ trust that has been established on behalf of SMTB for the purpose of facilitating lending and credit investment by SMTB in Australia and New Zealand, with a focus on private debt, bank loans, and specialty finance opportunities. The Trust will not carry out any lending prior to completion of the Acquisition.

The trustee of the Trust, Eticore SD Pty Ltd, and the investment manager, IFM Investors Pty Ltd, are both domiciled in Australia.

SMTB proposes to make a commitment into the Trust, in exchange for 100% of the units in the Trust. Post-acquisition, SMTB will be the only unitholder in the Trust, and will use the Trust to provide loans and credit investment in Australia and New Zealand.

determination_table_content.details:
Sumitomo Mitsui Trust Bank, Limited (SMTB) applied for a
notification waiver in respect of its proposed acquisition of 100% of
the units in the IFM SuMi TRUST ANZ Debt Fund (the Trust), as
described in the transaction documents provided as part of the
application (the Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABV(1)(a) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.

The acquirer, SMTB, is a Japanese-based provider of financial
services. In Australia, SMTB provides commercial lending services,
including general corporate loans, fund financing, and property
finance. SMTB’s commercial lending services are mainly conducted
through offshore booking transactions by SMTB’s Singapore Branch.
SMTB also provides ‘trust banking services’ to Australia-based
customers, which are a combination of traditional banking functions
and fiduciary services, with a particular focus on fee-based business
such as asset management and trust administration, often serving
long-term institutional clients.
The target, the Trust, is a ‘fund-of-one’ trust that has been
established for the purpose of facilitating lending and credit
investment by SMTB in Australia and New Zealand, with a focus on
private debt, bank loans, and specialty finance opportunities. The
Trust will not carry out any lending prior to completion of the
Acquisition.
The trustee of the Trust is Eticore SD Pty Ltd, and the investment
manager is IFM Investors Pty Ltd. Both entities are domiciled in
Australia and are an independent corporate trustee and investment
manager, respectively.
SMTB proposes to make a commitment into the Trust in exchange
for 100% of the units in the Trust. Post-acquisition, SMTB will be the
only unitholder in the Trust, and will use the Trust to provide loans
and credit investment in Australia and New Zealand.

In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application, and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers that
the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening of
competition. In particular:
a. the target has been established for the sole purpose of
facilitating lending and credit investment by SMTB in
Australia and New Zealand, and as such the Acquisition
does not result in any horizontal consolidation or the
removal of a competitor
b. there are alternative suppliers of commercial lending
services in Australia.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s interim guidance on
notification waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
